correctness.rationale: For any faithful module, S_v=sum incoming arrow images is killed by outgoing arrows because J^2=0; each m_uv-dimensional arrow space acts through Hom(M_u/S_u,S_v), forcing t_u*s_v>=m_uv and nonzero active s_v,t_u. Nonzero vertex idempotents force dim M_v>=1, so objective is a lower bound (inactive outgoing quotient may be set zero for optimization). Conversely choose split spaces S_v^0 and T_v^0, with isolated one-dimensional spaces, and assign distinct matrix units from T_u^0 to S_v^0 to individual arrows; products of arrows are zero and all idempotents+arrows linearly independent, over every field incl F2. For m<=2 every doubled arrow requires upgrade of tail t_u or head s_v, giving a vertex-cover constraint and unit cost, minimized by bipartite König matching. Independently checked exact brute integer optimum vs matching for 12501 one-, two- and three-vertex multiplicity matrices (entries 0..2), and constructed K_rr examples through r=4; infinite/all-field proof is algebraic not empirical.

value.rationale: Minimum faithful module dimension is a natural algebraic invariant measuring smallest unital matrix embedding. The all-field exact integer criterion and tractable matching formula for two-parallel-arrow quivers provide genuinely useful global structure and explicit quadratic-to-linear compression, not just restating representation-theoretic definitions.

final_claim: For finite quiver Q over arbitrary field k including loops and multiarrows, minimal faithful module dimension of A=kQ/J^2 is integer optimum sum_v max(1,s_v+t_v) under t_u*s_v >= m_uv and active incoming/outgoing lower bounds. When all m_uv<=2 it equals |Q0|+|H cap T|+nu(D_Q), where D_Q connects separate outgoing/incoming copies at doubly-arrowed ordered pairs. K_rr doubled-source-to-sink family has min degree 3r.
limitations: Closed matching formula only for multiplicities <=2; general multiplicities retain integer optimization.
Not an isomorphism classification of faithful modules; no new formal verification claim.
